utterances.text: I didn't have time to watch out for these things.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: How big was this window?

utterances.speaker: LJUBO PRIBUDIC
utterances.text: Well, how big the window was. What do I know how big it was?

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Well, you're in a basement. And I'm curious to know what kind of a window is in a basement room.

utterances.speaker: LJUBO PRIBUDIC
utterances.text: It was a basement room. How large may it have been?

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Your statement continues: "They first checked my details because they had my file in front of them. Then Goran Hadzic came into the room and said, And said to me, there you are, scalesman, you mother fucker. And then he slapped my face once. Then he did it again. Then he slapped my face as he turned around, and then he slapped me again and then he went out. Before that, he ordered me to squat down. Then he came in again and asked me whether Mladen Mrkic owed me something. And then he kicked me in the stomach and left the room. Five minutes later, he came back with a new question and he wanted to kick me between my legs, but I moved so he kicked me in the ribs. In the meantime, Stankovic interrogated me about a person with the last name of Madjar, what I knew about him. I remember that Goran Hadzic asked me where my sons were." And then you give a response. "And at that, Goran Hadzic spat in my face, went out and came back. And the person armed with a Kalashnikov told me, Do you want me to beat the crap out of you?" Now, Mr. Pribudic, this account of the interrogation looks a bit different than what you have testified to today. For one thing, it appears from your statement - and you can tell me if my reading is wrong - that Mr. Hadzic gives you four slaps in a row during his first entry into the room. When you read what you wrote there -- what you said was accurate and correct in August 2013, would you agree with my interpretation of what you did -- what you wrote down there?

utterances.speaker: LJUBO PRIBUDIC
utterances.text: No, it's not true. He didn't slap me four times then. He slapped me once, and then he asked, Which side did I slap you on? And then he slapped me on the other cheek. And -- but it's -- it is not the way you -- you said. Then there was this guy holding the - what's it called? - Kalashnikov or something. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Today you have specified that the only physical aggression by Mr. Hadzic against you was slapping and spitting. And here, in your statement from just three months ago, you say that he kicked you. That's not right, is it?

utterances.speaker: LJUBO PRIBUDIC
utterances.text: No, he didn't kick me in the stomach. He wanted to kick me between my legs, but then I moved, and he hit my ribs. So he didn't kick me in the belly. And he said, Now you're -- you're not going out in the next five years. And I replied, Well, it doesn't matter, as long as it's war, man. The food is good.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Gosnell, when I intervened about the slapping, the punching, just before that, the witness did speak about punching. So when you put to him that today he only speaks about slapping, I think you're missing the punching that you said you would ask about.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Well, I did follow up with that, Mr. President, because I asked whether he had ever been hit with a clenched fist. Because I didn't know whether the interpretation of the word "punch" was correct, so I followed up by asking whether he had been hit with a closed fist. And then when he said no, I understood that as a correction of his previous testimony. That was -- at least that was the purpose of the question and that was my understanding of the answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: So now, Mr. Pribudic, you're -- you're correcting or adding to your testimony and you're saying -- even though I asked you earlier whether there was any physical aggression by Mr. Hadzic against you other than being slapped and spat at, now you're telling us that he kicked you as well.

utterances.speaker: LJUBO PRIBUDIC
utterances.text: While he was turning around, he kicked me. But punching and slapping is not the same thing. You punch with a clenched fist.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Quite so. And am I right that you earlier told us that Mr. Hadzic never struck you with a clenched fist?

utterances.speaker: LJUBO PRIBUDIC
utterances.text: Why he didn't punch me. He slapped me. But you should ask him why he didn't punch me. When he was turning around, he slapped me on the head.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And you said that he was asking you about Mrkic. And you've testified that, in your words, Mrkic was Hadzic's director. Isn't it correct that Vupik is an organisation of about 400 employees with offices spread out in Eastern Slavonia with the headquarters in Vukovar? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: LJUBO PRIBUDIC
utterances.text: It is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And am I right that Vukic's office -- excuse me, that Mrkic's office was in the Eltz castle in Vukovar?

utterances.speaker: LJUBO PRIBUDIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And Mr. Hadzic was working in the Pacetin office of Vupik, which was very small. Five employees or less; correct?

utterances.speaker: LJUBO PRIBUDIC
utterances.text: Correct. I don't know if there were five exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And Mr. Hadzic was not even --

utterances.speaker: LJUBO PRIBUDIC
utterances.text: I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Mr. Hadzic was not even the head of that small branch of Vupik, was he?

utterances.speaker: LJUBO PRIBUDIC
utterances.text: I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: So when you say that Mrkic was Hadzic's director, you don't mean that he has any direct or ongoing supervision of Mr. Hadzic, based on your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: LJUBO PRIBUDIC
utterances.text: Director. Hadzic worked at Kooperacija, and it was an organisational unit of Vupik. What exactly he did, I don't know, but that one was a director and he was a warehouse keeper or something. But I don't know that. That's their problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: What I'm suggesting to you is that Mr. Hadzic does not have, based on your information, and I put this to you as a matter of my information, he has no close relationship at all with Mrkic. So do you have any indication as to why he's asking you questions about you -- or he owing money to you? Do you have any explanation for that?

utterances.speaker: LJUBO PRIBUDIC
utterances.text: Because Mrkic used to play poker with me, and he borrowed money frequently. How he knew about it, I don't know who told him. Mrkic borrowed money from me on a few occasions.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Any indication as to why Mr. Hadzic is preoccupied with that issue with you?

utterances.speaker: LJUBO PRIBUDIC
utterances.text: How should I know why he was preoccupied with that. He asked me about that at Mitrovica. Never before.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: I'd like to turn to a new subject --

utterances.speaker: LJUBO PRIBUDIC
utterances.text: He may have heard from ...

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed, Mr. Pribudic. Sorry, Mr. Pribudic, I didn't mean to interrupt. Did you want to add something?

utterances.speaker: LJUBO PRIBUDIC
utterances.text: I don't know why he asked me whether that one owed me money. I don't know how he found out about his borrowings from me. We were good pals and we played cards together and that -- all that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: I'd like to move to -- to back up and talk about your arrest before you went to Velepromet on the 18th of November.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Gosnell, would that be your last topic?

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Mr. President, it is the last topic, but what I would request, if possible, is an opportunity to consult with client before concluding my cross. If that means breaking early, I'm more than happy to do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Mr. Pribudic, who put you under arrest and took you to Velepromet on the 18th of November? Could you identify the people who did that, either based on uniforms or recognising them --

utterances.speaker: LJUBO PRIBUDIC
utterances.text: The JNA, the army.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And did they walk you over to Velepromet in a group?

utterances.speaker: LJUBO PRIBUDIC
utterances.text: The army was dressed in olive-drab military uniforms. My wife and I walked up to the park, and then they put us on a truck that took us to the Velepromet yard. Those were -- those people were unknown to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Was that a civilian or a military truck, from what you could see of it?

utterances.speaker: LJUBO PRIBUDIC
utterances.text: It was a civilian truck, the one that took me there.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And was that civilian truck escorted by any JNA vehicles to Velepromet?

utterances.speaker: LJUBO PRIBUDIC
utterances.text: It was on the road, but if it was escorted or not, I don't know. They probably used it for transporting those that were older and weaker. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And did you continue to -- or did you observe JNA soldiers bringing more prisoners to Velepromet while you were there, or did you hear that that was going on?

utterances.speaker: LJUBO PRIBUDIC
utterances.text: No, I never heard anything and didn't observe. I had no time to watch out for people coming or going. I was preoccupied with my own ordeal.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And you say that you were taken in a bus from Velepromet to the JNA barracks late on the evening of the 21st of November. Can you describe that scene as to how you came to leave the barracks and enter the bus?

utterances.speaker: LJUBO PRIBUDIC
utterances.text: We were waiting in the morning, and then they opened the gates and told us, Come on, get on the buses. And we went toward the buses, but we didn't know what would happen. And then the bus started moving towards Negoslavci and continued to Mitrovica.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Sorry, Mr. Pribudic, I'm not talking now about the bus between Vukovar barracks and Sremska Mitrovica. I'm asking you about boarding the bus at Velepromet that took you to the JNA barracks. Can you describe that scene and, in particular, did you see any JNA soldiers or officers present on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: LJUBO PRIBUDIC
utterances.text: That's something else. That was not your question. You're asking that only now. There was a -- an officer with a high rank, and he said, Come on, get out and get on the buses. Chetniks will come and slaughter you all. And we boarded the buses, which took us to the barracks.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Did you observe any contention or disagreement between the soldiers who were -- or the people who were guarding you at Velepromet and the JNA officer?

utterances.speaker: LJUBO PRIBUDIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't notice anything. But I wasn't paying attention either. I was only looking down.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And other than this JNA officer with a high rank, did you see other JNA soldiers, including JNA military police?

utterances.speaker: LJUBO PRIBUDIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't. He was just standing there and yelling, Come on, come on, move. And -- that officer I mean.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Mr. President, I -- I would conclude my cross-examination subject to an opportunity to consult with my client. If -- if perhaps it wouldn't be too much trouble to perhaps take the break --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Take the break now? Okay. We'll take the break. We'll take the break and let's come back at -- well, let's come back at 12.45 as -- as usual. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Gosnell.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Just a few very brief questions, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Mr. Pribudic, were you sitting in a chair throughout your interview or throughout this interrogation that we've been discussing?

utterances.speaker: LJUBO PRIBUDIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And when you --

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Mr. President --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Are we -- are we sure that we're talking about the same thing here? Because I was a little bit confused.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Mr. Pribudic, maybe I should make my question absolutely clear to you. I'm asking you whether, during the interrogation, in which Mr. Hadzic enters the room several times, were you seated throughout that interview or interrogation?

utterances.speaker: LJUBO PRIBUDIC
utterances.text: I wasn't seated at all. I was either standing or squatting. Actually, I was squatting, almost the whole time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stringer.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: With -- with respect, it seemed to me that the question as rephrased was a bit ambiguous because one could be seated without sitting in a chair, which was the -- I mean, one could be seated on the floor, in theory. So it seemed there was a bit of a shift that could have been ambiguous for the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Well, at least one ambiguity has been clarified. And let's see what the exact answer was. I think the answer is clear enough, Mr. Stringer. You agree? Please proceed, Mr. Gosnell.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And when you spoke to Mr. Cakalic and he told you that he had been interrogated by Mr. Hadzic, did he tell you, at that time, whether Mr. Hadzic held any position?

utterances.speaker: LJUBO PRIBUDIC
utterances.text: No, he didn't tell me anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Did you learn what -- Mr. Hadzic's position sometime soon after your release from Sremska Mitrovica prison?

utterances.speaker: LJUBO PRIBUDIC
utterances.text: I learned that he was the president of the SAO Krajina. So I was in the habit of saying that I had had the honour of being slapped by the president of Krajina.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And you were in the habit of saying that to whom?

utterances.speaker: LJUBO PRIBUDIC
utterances.text: To my family members, at home. Nothing official.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And you didn't bring this experience of yours to the attention of any authorities in Croatia for 18 years; is that right?

utterances.speaker: LJUBO PRIBUDIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't. That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And did you --

utterances.speaker: LJUBO PRIBUDIC
utterances.text: I thought that -- let bygones be bygones.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Did you ever hear from the media or from your friends that there were, in fact, criminal proceedings against Mr. Hadzic ongoing as early as 1992 in Croatia?

utterances.speaker: LJUBO PRIBUDIC
utterances.text: I wasn't following that. I heard on TV and read in newspapers that there was a proceeding going on, but I didn't think that I should get involved in that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Pribudic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Mr. President, that concludes my cross-examination. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Stringer, anything in re-direct?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: No -- No, Your Honour. No re-direct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Pribudic, this is the end of your testimony for the Tribunal. Thank you very much for assisting us. You are now released as a witness --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You're welcome.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: I wish you a safe journey home. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Gosnell.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Gosnell.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Sorry, Mr. President there is one more thing I should have done, and I don't believe it involves the witness. But we would request to tender 06487, being the witness's prior statement from the 5th of August, 2013.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: The purpose being, Mr. Gosnell?

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: In this particular case, we would ask that you admit this particular statement because there are sequences of events that are described, and we say that the sequence is not in line with the sequence that was described by the witness. I did put the passages, and yet there's really no way to fully assess the significance of the sequence without the full context. And I would also suggest that even if I did read in everything that was relevant, there's actually no concrete evidence as to what the witness said or the nature of his affirmation unless you admit the statement. So, on those grounds, I would --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Resolve inconsistency.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Precisely. Yes -- oh, certainly the purpose of admission is purely to -- for credibility.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Stringer.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: We object to it, Mr. President. The position is that counsel has had ample time to explore any inconsistencies with the witness, and it is not only inconsistency but there is consistency as well. And if it is going to be admitted, then let's admit it for all purposes in this unique situation. But it seems only half of it -- to tender a statement only for the limited purpose here, when counsel's had full opportunity on cross to bring out inconsistencies, it's certainly not in line with what's largely been the practice in this case, not admit statements when there has been full cross-examination. If the Chamber is minded to admit it, however, the Prosecution submits it should be admitted for all purposes. Having said that, of course, the witness hasn't really adopted it in a way that a witness would be adopting a 92 ter statement. He's said that there are things in there such as the date of his release which are incorrect. And so again it's -- the value of it, outside of the cross-examination that the Chamber already has, I think is limited. But, in any event, it is unfair to admit it only for impeachment and we therefore object.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Mr. President, I promise I won't repeat any of my submissions, but just on the issue of the purpose of admission, the practice of the Tribunal is clear that prior inconsistent statements can be admitted for the limited purpose of impeachment. And 92 ter is the manner by which prior statements are admitted for the substance of the content.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Stringer, the fault may be entirely mine that I'm confused, but when you say that if it is admitted -- it should be admitted for all purposes but then you go on to say that he hasn't adopted it in the way that a witness adopts a 92 ter statement, aren't you walking in opposite directions on the point?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: I think in the end what would happen is the parties, both of them, would in equality be free to point out inconsistencies as well as consistencies; that is, things contained in the statement which the witness has affirmed today in his viva voce evidence. And so that's the point I was attempting to make. In terms of practice, my reference was not so much to Tribunal practice but the practice that's been utilised -- I believe I'm correct in this, the Chamber has tended not admit statements for impeachment purposes when there's been full opportunity to cross-examination. I believe a proposed interlocutory appeal was even denied on that issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: The document is admitted and marked for the purpose mentioned by the Defence.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, 65 ter 6487 receives number Exhibit D105.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: This -- this document, this is the document with the revised translation under 6487.2; right?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: That's my understanding, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Okay. So --

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Although --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: -- then OTP will replace the previous translation by the current one?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: If possible, Your Honour, because this was just made available to us this morning in the courtroom, we would like to have an opportunity to review it before we take a position on substituting it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Let's -- would it be okay if we say that you take a position by, let's say, Wednesday, end of -- close of business? Would --

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Absolutely, Mr. President. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. If there's nothing else, court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: sine die.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.03 p.m.,
